comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of the 2024 Restructuring Plan, which focused on driving efficiencies and aligning resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD announced specific 2024 Restructuring Plans focused on cost reduction and operational efficiency. Intel's plan, announced in Q3 2024, targets headcount and expenditure cuts with substantial completion expected by Q4 2025. AMD also implemented a 2024 Restructuring Plan in 2024, recognizing $186 million in charges, specifically aiming to drive efficiencies and align resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets.

sentences.text: In Q3 2024, the 2024 Restructuring Plan was announced, subsequently approved and committed to by our management team, and initiated to implement cost-reduction measures, including reductions in employee headcount, other operating expenditures, and capital expenditures (see "Note 7: Restructuring and Other Charges" within Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements).

We expect that our 2024 Restructuring Plan, in conjunction with other initiatives, will reduce our cost structure while we continue our investments to develop, manufacture, market, sell, and deliver product and process initiatives in furtherance of our strategy.
We recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of a restructuring plan (the 2024 Restructuring Plan).
The 2024 Restructuring Plan was focused on driving efficiencies across the business and aligning resources with our largest growth opportunities in the AI and enterprise markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: While both companies recognized significant restructuring charges in 2024, the drivers differed. Intel’s restructuring was a broad cost-reduction plan including headcount and capex cuts. Broadcom’s $1,533 million in restructuring charges were primarily attributed to employee termination costs associated with the VMware Merger, whereas Intel's charges were part of a broader operational realignment rather than a single merger event.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company implemented cost reduction measures including a restructuring plan that reduced headcount by approximately 15%, incurred $171 million in restructure charges, and achieved estimated quarterly savings of $130 million through 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies implemented major restructuring efforts to reduce headcount and costs, but the timing differed. Intel initiated its 2024 Restructuring Plan in Q3 2024. In contrast, Micron's relevant restructuring plan was the '2023 Restructure Plan,' which was substantially completed in 2023 and resulted in a 15% headcount reduction; Micron noted in 2024 that it was phasing out temporary cost-saving measures from that 2023 plan rather than announcing a new 2024 plan.

sentences.text: In Q3 2024, the 2024 Restructuring Plan was announced, subsequently approved and committed to by our management team, and initiated to implement cost-reduction measures, including reductions in employee headcount, other operating expenditures, and capital expenditures (see "Note 7: Restructuring and Other Charges" within Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements).
We expect actions pursuant to the 2024 Restructuring Plan to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of 2025, which is subject to change.
Under the 2023 Restructure Plan, we reduced our headcount by approximately 15% by the end of calendar 2023, through a combination of voluntary attrition and personnel reductions.

The 2023 Restructure Plan, which was substantially completed in 2023, yielded estimated cost savings of approximately $130 million per quarter (approximately 60% in cost of goods sold, 30% in R&D, and 10% in SG&A) subsequent to 2023.
